newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity lower on generation boost, temps.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity lower on generation boost, temps.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were lower Friday in relatively quiet trade taking weakness from increased power generation and some below normal temperatures in the U.S. West, industry sources said.
"In general the generation is coming back (in the West) and they seem to be getting a little break in the weather," said one New York-based futures trader.

As of 12505 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was down $1.55 at $31.55 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $31.25-32.40, while September was down $1.07 at the day's low of $27.35 after trade as high as $27.90 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 61 cents at $22.20 after trades at $22.10-22.50, while September was trading down 46 cents at the day's low of $22.25 following exchange as high as $22.45 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1210 EDT an estimated total of 74 COB and 356 PV contracts had traded.

Temperatures through the Pacific Northwest were forecast to be cooler-than-normal into early next week, while the Southwest was expected to see temperatures one to three degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the south and west and near normal elsewhere over the next several days.
In additional to weather, rising power supply in the West was seen putting downward pressure on the futures and Western cash power prices.

Electricity output at the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California was reduced to 90 percent of capacity early Friday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily plant status report.
The adjoining 1,080 MW unit 3 was expected to resume operations around July 10 after being taken offline April 12 for refueling.

The WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state continued to await clearance from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission before beginning start-up operations, a spokesman for the plant said Thursday, adding the unit would be "physically ready" to resume operations by late tonight or early Friday.

Several Western coal-fired power units were also expected to return to the power grid over the next several days, including a 670 MW unit at Centralia, Wash., a 330 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado.
As of 1250 EDT, August NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas was trading down 0.4 cents at $2.119 per million British thermal units.

Separately, the board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council is expected to vote today on a summer derating of the Pacific Intertie transmission system to 6,300 MW from the current 7,200 MW, beginning in early July.
